```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

## Problem 1

```{r clean_subway_data}
nyc_transit_df =
  read_csv("data/NYC_Transit_Subway_Entrance_And_Exit_Data.csv") %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  select(line, station_name, station_latitude, station_longitude, starts_with("route"), entry, vending, entrance_type, ada) %>%
  mutate(
    entry = case_match(entry, "YES" ~ TRUE, "NO" ~ FALSE)
  )
```
This dataset contains information about NYC subway station and their entrances and exits. The key variables include station information, such as line and station name. Geographic location, such as station latitude and station longitude. Routes served, entrance detial, and accessibility status.
For data cleaning, I first cleaned the column names using `janitor::clean_names()` to make them easier to work with. Next, I used `select()` to keep only the required variables. Then, I converted the entry variable from character values into logical values using the `case_match()` function. The resulting dataset has `r nrow(nyc_transit_df)` and `r ncol(nyc_transit_df)` clomns.
But this dataset is not tidy. The main reason is that the route information is spread across eleven different columns. To make the data tidy, each route variable should be reshaped into a single column so that each row represents a unique observation.

**How many distinct stations are there?**
```{r subway}
distinct_stations = nyc_transit_df %>%
  distinct(line, station_name) %>%
  nrow()
```
There are `r distinct_stations` distinct station in there.

**How many stations are ADA compliant?**
```{r}
ada_compliant_stations = nyc_transit_df %>%
  filter(ada == TRUE) %>%
  distinct(line, station_name) %>%
  nrow()
```
There are `r ada_compliant_stations` ada compliant.

**What proportion of station entrances / exits without vending allow entrance?**
```{r}
vending_no_prop = nyc_transit_df %>%
  filter(vending == "NO") %>%
  summarize(prop = mean(entry)) %>%
  pull(prop)
```
The proportion of station entrances / exits without vending allow entrance is about `r round(vending_no_prop, 3)` .

**Reformat data**
```{r}
subway_reformat_df = nyc_transit_df %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("route"), as.character)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("route"),
    names_to = "route_number",
    names_prefix = "route",
    values_to = "route_name"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(route_name))
```

```{r}
A_train = subway_reformat_df %>%
  filter(route_name == "A") %>%
  distinct(line, station_name) %>%
  nrow()
```
There are `r A_train` distinct stations that serve the A train.

```{r}
A_train_ada = subway_reformat_df %>%
  filter(route_name == "A", ada == TRUE) %>%
  distinct(line, station_name) %>%
  nrow()
```
There are `r A_train_ada` are ada compliant.

## Problem 2
```{r}
library(readxl)
```

```{r Mr_Trash_Wheel}
Mr_Trash_Wheel = 
  read_excel("data/202610 Trash Wheel Collection Data.xlsx",
             sheet = "Mr. Trash Wheel",
             skip = 1
                            ) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  filter(!is.na(dumpster)) %>%
  select(-starts_with("x")) %>%
  mutate(
    sports_balls = as.integer(round(sports_balls)),
    year = as.numeric(year),
    wheel = "Mr. Trash Wheel"
  )
```

```{r Professor_Trash_Wheel, warning = FALSE}
Professor_Trash_Wheel = 
  read_excel("data/202610 Trash Wheel Collection Data.xlsx",
             sheet = "Professor Trash Wheel",
             skip = 1) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  filter(!is.na(dumpster)) %>%
  select(-starts_with("x")) %>%
  mutate(
    plastic_bottles = as.numeric(plastic_bottles),
    year = as.numeric(year),
    wheel = "Professor Trash Wheel"
  )
```

```{r Gwynnda_Trash_Wheel}
gwynnda_trash_wheel = 
  read_excel("data/202610 Trash Wheel Collection Data.xlsx",
             sheet = "Gwynnda the Good Wheel of the W",
             skip = 1) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  filter(!is.na(dumpster)) %>%
  select(-starts_with("x")) %>%
  mutate(
    plastic_bottles = as.numeric(plastic_bottles),
    year = as.numeric(year),
    wheel = "Gwynnda the Good Wheel of the W"
  )
```

```{r produce a single tidy dataset}
all_trash_wheel = bind_rows(Mr_Trash_Wheel, Professor_Trash_Wheel, gwynnda_trash_wheel) %>%
  relocate(wheel)
```

**what was the total weight of trash collected by Professor Trash Wheel?**
```{r}
Professor_Trash_Weight = all_trash_wheel %>%
  filter(wheel == "Professor Trash Wheel") %>%
  summarize(total_weight = sum(weight_tons, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(total_weight)
```

**What was the total number of cigarette butts collected by Gwynnda in June of 2022?**
```{r}
gwynnda_june2022_cigs = all_trash_wheel %>%
  filter(wheel == "Gwynnda the Good Wheel of the W", year == 2022, month == "June") %>%
  summarize(total_cigs = sum(cigarette_butts, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(total_cigs)
```
This combined dataset contains a total of `r nrow(all_trash_wheel)` observations across `r ncol(all_trash_wheel)` variables, merging records from Mr Trash Wheel, Professor Trash Wheel, and Gwynnda. Key variables in the dataset include the vessel identifier (`wheel`), dumpster numbers (`dumpster`), collection dates (`date`), total trash weight in tons (`weight_tons`), trash volume (`volume_cubic_yards`), and specific litter categories such as `plastic_bottles`, `polystyrene`, and `cigarette_butts`.
Based on the available data, the total weight of trash collected by Professor Trash Wheel was `r Professor_Trash_Weight` tons. In addition, the total number of cigarette butts collected by Gwynnda in June of 2022 was `r format(gwynnda_june2022_cigs, scientific = FALSE)`.

## Problem 3
```{r}
mci_baseline_df = read_csv("data/data_mci/MCI_baseline.csv", skip = 1, na = c(".", "NA", "")) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  mutate(
    sex = case_match(sex, 1 ~ "male", 0 ~ "female"),
    apoe4 = case_match(apoe4, 1 ~ "carrier", 0 ~ "non-carrier")
  ) %>%
  filter(is.na(age_at_onset) | age_at_onset > current_age)
```
**How many participants were recruited, and of these how many develop MCI? What is the average baseline age? What proportion of women in the study are APOE4 carriers?**
```{r}
n_recruited = nrow(mci_baseline_df)

n_mci = mci_baseline_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(age_at_onset)) %>%
  nrow()

mean_age = mci_baseline_df %>%
  pull(current_age) %>%
  mean()

prop_female_apoe4 = mci_baseline_df %>%
  filter(sex == "female") %>%
  summarize(prop = mean(apoe4 == "carrier")) %>%
  pull(prop)
```
To clean the baseline demographic dataset, the first row containing column descriptions was skipped during import, and missing values represented by `.` were parsed as `NA`. Categorical indicators were recoded: `sex` was converted to `male`/`female`, and `apoe4` status was recoded to `carrier`/`non-carrier`. Participants who already had MCI at or prior to baseline (`age_at_onset <= current_age`) were removed to meet the inclusion criteria.
A total of `r n_recruited` participants were eligible at baseline. Of these, `r n_mci` participants developed MCI during the follow-up period. The average baseline age of the participants was `r round(mean_age, 1)` years. Among the female participants, approximately `r round(prop_female_apoe4 * 100, 1)`% were APOE4 carriers.

```{r amyloid}
mci_amyloid_df = read_csv("data/data_mci/mci_amyloid.csv", skip = 1, na = c("Na", "NA", "", ".")) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  rename(id = study_id)
n_amyloid = nrow(mci_amyloid_df)
```
For the amyloid dataset, the file was imported skipping the introductory header line, and missing observations labeled as `Na` were recoded to `NA`. The `study_id` variable was renamed to `id` to align with the baseline demographic dataset. The dataset tracks the amyloid 42/40 ratio over multiple visits across `r n_amyloid` individuals.

```{r combin}
only_baseline = anti_join(mci_baseline_df, mci_amyloid_df, by = "id") %>%
  nrow()

only_amyloid = anti_join(mci_amyloid_df, mci_baseline_df, by = "id") %>%
  nrow()

mci_both_df = inner_join(mci_baseline_df, mci_amyloid_df, by = "id")

write_csv(mci_both_df, "data/mci_both.csv")
```
When comparing the two datasets, `r only_baseline` participants appear only in the baseline demographic cohort, indicating they either lacked biomarker measurements or were lost to follow-up before amyloid collection. Conversely, `r only_amyloid` participants were present in the amyloid dataset but omitted from the baseline analysis, likely due to failing the baseline inclusion criteria (having MCI at baseline) or missing demographic files.

Merging both datasets using an inner join yields a final dataset of `r nrow(mci_both_df)` participants with both demographic features and longitudinal biomarker measurements across `r ncol(mci_both_df)` variables. The tidied dataset was exported as `mci_both.csv` in the project's data directory.
